approved.en: Ukraine is intensifying its strike campaign, using naval drones to hit Russian warships in Libya’s Benghazi port and launching more long-range attacks in 2026 than earlier in the war, while Russian drone strikes continue to damage Ukraine’s energy, rail and civilian infrastructure, killing civilians. Russia has also violated Finnish airspace with a helicopter and Polish airspace with an unmanned aerial vehicle, prompting NATO to pledge defence against a reported Russian space threat. The UN Security Council warned that winter attacks on Ukraine’s power grid and Black Sea shipping threaten lives and global food supplies. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
approved.nb: Ukraina intensiverer sin angrepskampanje, bruker marine-droner for å treffe russiske krigsskip i Benghazi-havnen i Libya og gjennomfører flere langdistanseangrep i 2026 enn tidligere i krigen, mens russiske droneangrep fortsetter å skade Ukrainas energi‑, jernbane‑ og sivile infrastruktur, og dreper sivile. Russland har også krenket finsk luftrom med en helikopter og polsk luftrom med et ubemannet luftfartøy, noe som får NATO til å love forsvar mot en rapportert russisk romtrussel. FNs sikkerhetsråd advarte om at vinterangrep på Ukrainas strømnett og skipsfart i Svartehavet truer liv og global matforsyning. Konflikten forårsaket 75 767 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

approved.en: Israel has intensified airstrikes and artillery shelling on southern Lebanon, targeting Hezbollah rocket sites, launchers in the Beqaa Valley, and other facilities, while drones have flown over Beirut. Hezbollah is reportedly using fishing boats to spy on the Israeli navy and Israel is employing Christian villages in south Lebanon in a divide-and-conquer effort. Hezbollah’s leader has again demanded the release of five detained operatives and rejected any post-UNIFIL force outside U.N. authority, as both sides prepare for an eighth round of peace talks before year-end. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ifølge rapporter bruker Hizbollah fiskebåter til å spionere på den israelske marinen, og Israel bruker kristne landsbyer i Sør-Lebanon i en del-og-hersk-strategi. Hizbollahs leder har igjen krevd løslatelse av fem fengslede operatører og avvist enhver styrke etter UNIFIL utenfor FN myndighet, mens begge sider forbereder den åttende runden med fredssamtaler før årsskiftet. Ifølge UCDP har konflikten forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024.

Foreign troops are beginning to withdraw, raising concerns that al-Shabaab could expand its influence. The United States has reversed its funding for international military support to Somalia. approved.en: Thailand is confronting multiple security and environmental pressures, including a bomb explosion in its southern region that prompted police to tighten border security and the air force to scramble F-16s, and an explosion at an oil facility in Bangkok that injured nine people. The government is also facing cross-border tensions as Cambodia formally protested a Thai road expansion in Oddar Meanchey and both countries agreed to a UN-backed maritime site visit, while Thailand and Myanmar are pressing each other over arsenic contamination from Shan State mines. Mining pollution is disrupting the Festival of Lights and prompting joint monitoring efforts, and a Japanese aid worker called for better integration of Myanmar migrants. Regjeringen møter også grenseoverskridende spenninger ettersom Kambodsja formelt protesterte mot en thailandsk veiutvidelse i Oddar Meanchey, og begge land ble enige om et FN-støttet maritimt stedbesøk, mens Thailand og Myanmar presser hverandre om arsenikkforurensning fra gruver i Shan-delstaten. Gruveforurensning forstyrrer Festivalen av lys og fører til felles overvåkningstiltak, og en japansk hjelpearbeider oppfordret til bedre integrering av Myanmar-migranter. approved.en: Venezuela disclosed a $237.5 billion debt pile and began a large restructuring while the United States signed a security cooperation pact with the interim Venezuelan government, after which a U.S. marine died falling overboard during a Caribbean operation linked to the renewed ties. The Senate is probing JD Vance for allegedly steering a Venezuelan oil license to Vitol and another senator’s role in the same deal, while Citi is weighing a market re-entry after a five-year exit. Venezuelan authorities later declared the security pact null and void, illegal gold mining continues, and Eni and Repsol pledged a $2 billion joint-venture investment. According to UCDP, there were 2 battle-related deaths in 2007.
